details: False for finite classes under the message-free definition. On #classes/balanced_six_split, proper equivalence-query complexity is 3 but no proper unlabeled compression scheme exists, even without stability. Thus psUSC is $+\infty$, and no finite-valued function of $Q_{\mathrm{peq}}$ universally bounds psUSC. This does not settle the comparison restricted to classes admitting proper stable unlabeled schemes.
proof_source: Survey Corollary cor:balanced-six-split-nonexistence, using Proposition prop:proper-unlabeled-pair-obstruction and the database-owned benchmark proofs.
witness_verification: Values 1183 and 1185 give $Q_{\mathrm{peq}}=3$ and $\mathrm{psUSC}=+\infty$. Nonexistence on this fixed finite class refutes every finite upper bound, in particular every proposed affine bound. This is stronger than a growing finite ratio and is not an asymptotic-family claim.
name: Proper Equivalence Queries Complexity / Proper Stable Sample Compression
